en.title: Stock Profit Pairs Deduplicated by Value
en.description:
Count the unordered value pairs that can be formed from two distinct indices and sum to target. The same value pair counts only once; (a,a) requires at least two a.

The standard I/O and solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n target (1≤n≤500000, 0≤target≤5×10⁹); the second line contains n profits (0..10⁹).
en.explanation: Example 1: only (3,9) and (6,6), so the answer is 2. Example 2: a single 6 cannot pair with itself, so the answer is 0. Example 3: three 0s give three index pairs, but the only value pair is (0,0), so the answer is 1.
hints: Count frequencies and enumerate each distinct a, counting only when a≤target−a and the complement exists; when the two are equal, check that the frequency is at least 2.
